strengths: Strong theoretical analysis formalizing attention dispersion and proving α-entmax maintains bounded entropy O(log s) vs softmax's O(log n), with rigorous proofs of representational preservation and over-squashing alleviation
Impressive synthetic task results with 1000× length extrapolation on MQMTAR (76.7% at 65K tokens) and 8× on Reverse, demonstrating consistent improvements across retrieval, memory, and ordering tasks

Well-motivated innovations with ASEntmax's δ + β(log n)^γ scaling grounded in extreme value statistics and empirically validated to be naturally learned (Figure 4), plus sensible NAPE positional encoding design

Exceptionally thorough experimental analysis with comprehensive ablations across positional encodings, detailed per-task breakdown, and extensive supplementary material (40+ pages) enabling reproducibility
Clear, well-structured presentation with logical flow from theory to methods to experiments, good use of visualizations (attention maps, gradient norms)
weaknesses: Critically limited practical validation: all core experiments on 2-10M parameter synthetic tasks with only tangential LM experiment (120M on 5B tokens for learning parameters), no evaluation at realistic LLM scales (7B-70B), failing to demonstrate transfer from synthetic benchmarks to real-world settings

Computational efficiency analysis absent: α-entmax requires iterative threshold computation vs single softmax pass, yet no wall-clock time comparisons, memory overhead analysis, or concrete AdaSplash timing data provided despite being essential for practical adoption

Statistical rigor issues: results report 'best checkpoint from 3 random seeds' without error bars or significance tests, risking inflated numbers through cherry-picking; no confidence intervals or explicit reporting of all runs

ASEntmax introduces significant complexity (head-specific and query-specific learned parameters β, γ with softplus/tanh activations) with limited ablation justifying design choices and missing sensitivity analysis for hyperparameter robustness

Limited baseline comparisons: missing structured sparse attention methods (sliding windows, local attention, dilated patterns), Longformer and BigBird mentioned but not compared, restricting evaluation to softmax variants only

Questionable theoretical assumptions: Gaussian logit assumption (Remark 1) may not hold after multiple non-linear layers, independence assumptions in proofs acknowledged as violated, layer normalization approximated as constant—impacts real-world validity

Incomplete problem analysis: Sort task shows poor generalization (≤4×) across all methods without explanation, task selection appears somewhat arbitrary, deeper analysis of when/why methods fail missing
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned, ASEntmax complexity with per-head-per-query parameters makes implementation challenging, AdaSplash integration details missing

strengths: Strong theoretical analysis of α-entmax addressing fundamental softmax limitations (Lemma 1, Propositions 1-2) with rigorous proofs
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse synthetic tasks and language modeling with multiple baselines and positional encodings
Impressive synthetic task results: 1000× length extrapolation on MQMTAR (95.3% at 65K tokens), 96.4% on Reverse task
Practical ASEntmax method compatible with optimized kernels; head-specific learnable parameters provide flexibility
Thorough documentation and reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, extensive appendices, promised code release
Clear problem formulation with well-motivated identification of three softmax limitations
weaknesses: Limited novelty: α-entmax is from Peters et al. (2019); main contribution is application plus adaptive scaling design that appears somewhat ad-hoc
Theory-practice gap: Propositions rely on strong assumptions (bounded logits, specific support growth); theory justifies α-entmax but not why ASEntmax specifically works
Modest improvements on real-world language modeling: Table 3 shows ~10% perplexity improvement over SSMax; improvements often marginal and task-dependent
Critical dependence on NAPE (NoPE + ALiBi) that is not fully justified theoretically, making it difficult to isolate ASEntmax contribution
ASEntmax design lacks principled justification: parameterization δ + β(log n)^γ relies on IID Gaussian assumption; choice of softplus/tanh activation arbitrary; limited ablations
Scalability questions: largest model only 420M parameters; training context 2K tokens (moderate); no wall-clock time or memory analysis despite α-entmax computational overhead
Short-context performance sometimes degrades (Table 2: Lambada PPL 41.6 vs 48.9); results suggest method is sensitive to task-specific configurations
Missing comparisons with other sparse attention methods and recent long-context approaches; no visualization of learned attention patterns
